readme: HEARTROT arena geometry. The two rooms are PAINTINGS (assets/rooms/lobby.png and
assets/rooms/arena.png, committed verbatim) and `grid` is GENERATED from them:
python3 tools/gen_rooms.py writes it from the shapes in `rooms`, then
python3 tools/gen_map.py compiles it into programs/heartrot/src/map.rs and
packages/client/src/map.ts. Never hand-edit the grid or either of those two files.
To move a wall, re-measure the painting: edit `rooms` and re-run both tools.
`rooms` is measured in the PIXELS of each painting. Rects are {x, y, w, h}, the
ellipse {cx, cy, rx, ry}, tiles [col, row]. gen_rooms.py --check proves the grid and
app/src/render/rooms.gen.ts still match; docs/art/rooms/overlay-*.png is the human check.
lobby.floor_px        the walkable cobbles, a UNION of rects: the centre x 344..1351,
y 529..955 (the seat fan `player::lobby_spawn` deals, 208..664 on
row 52, needs col 13 -- which is why it reaches 51 px into the
pen's right rail), plus the two upper wings x 126..344 / 1351..1569
down to y 745, above the pen and the tent, which are furniture.
lobby.gates_px        the three doorways by tier (0 EASY, 1 MEDIUM, 2 HARD, left to
right), each cut out to gate<tier>.png and painted throat-dark in
lobby.png; each x-span is one G block on the gate rows.
lobby.lights_px       [x, y, r]: the painted torches (and the campfire), the glow radius
in px; their colours are read off the paint by gen_rooms.py.
arena.platform_ellipse_px  the dais the raid fights on; the WHOLE ellipse is the pit,
mirror-symmetrised about the centre line. The boss's body is not
cut out of it: player.rs refuses a step into the hitbox fold.
arena.stairs_px       the stairs down to the gate, so the pit reaches the rim.
arena.boss_crop_px    the boss's sprite canvas, cut by tools/gen_boss.py: centred on
the boss tile's pixel (561, 356) with even w/h, and taller than
the paint so the canvas centre is the FEET line (padded below).
arena.boss_tile       `B`, tile (32, 22): BOSS_SPAWN (512, 352), the creature's feet line
inside the pit band, and the anchor every row is derived from --
the arena painting is 1 px per unit with the boss's feet on this
tile, so its bottom edge is the rim (row 38), the gates are the two
rows under it, the lobby the rows under those, and the pit's first
row is the first whole row under the dais's crest (row 12).
arena.wall_bay_px     the back wall's pillar pitch (the braziers stand at 166, 429, 690,
951): gen_rooms.py fills the wall behind the demon one bay over.
arena.lights_px       [x, y, r]: the painted braziers, as lobby.lights_px.
arena.entrances_tiles the four `E` respawn doors, mirror pairs; each fans five ranks
along y, so the three rows above and below must be pit too.
Layout, top to bottom:
y=0        top border wall, ONE tile: the boss's crown is hittable above the pit.
y=1..23    OPEN FLOOR, the boss's air, cols 2..61: above the dais, and beside its
shoulders down to the row above its widest one. `shoot`'s raycast tests
`is_wall` before the part rectangles, so one wall tile here kills every shot
in that column -- and wall over a shoulder tile was a stand from which every
upward shot died. A raider may not stand on it: map::DAIS, a movement rule.
y=12..37   `P` pit: the whole dais ellipse plus the stairs, 1198 tiles (P, B, E), laid
over the air. The bounding rows emit PIT_TOP/PIT_BOT; the tiles emit DAIS.
y=38..39   `G` gates, three blocks with wall between: cols 12..18 EASY, 29..34 MEDIUM,
45..51 HARD (tier = block order, left to right). `enter_gate` demands you
stand in one and reads the tier off it; the gate is a portal, not a stair.
y=40..55   the lobby, the painted floor: cols 5..58 on rows 40..47, cols 11..52 on
rows 48..55 (the pen and the tent sit in the lower corners). ZERO interior
walls -- the barrels, cages, torches and floor markings inside the floor are
ART ONLY. The band is 16 rows because that is the painting's proportion at
LOBBY_HEAD 20 / LOBBY_FOOT 5 (viewport.ts); gen_rooms.py derives it.
y=56..62   wall: the bottom wall and the painting's foot.
y=63       bottom border wall.
gen_map.py still refuses a map whose entrances cannot reach the heart, whose spawn
points sit in a wall or off the dais, whose gate rows do not carry exactly N_TIERS
separate solid-rectangle G blocks (no two sharing a column) inside the lobby box, whose
dais is pinched in two or has wall directly over any tile, whose rows are not
mirror-symmetric, whose gate tiles a lobby spawn cannot walk to inside the lobby box,
whose G blocks are not rooms.gen.ts's LOBBY_GATES, whose heart stands on a gate, that
leaves any position in either zone with no legal move, or that carries a free-standing
obstacle off the gate rows. It no longer asks a gate to sit under the pit: the gate is
a portal (enter_gate writes entrance_for), so the blocks owe the dais no adjacency.

legend.P: floor, pit - the raider box; the P bounding rows emit PIT_TOP/PIT_BOT
legend.G: floor, gate - one of three blocks enter_gate demands, left to right = tier; emits GATES
legend.E: floor, entrance - a respawn door, must flood-fill to the heart
legend.B: floor, heart of the chamber - the boss spawn tile

readme: The secret room behind the lobby's WEST door, in TILES: [col, row, cols, rows] or [col, row].
A third zone, ZONE_SECRET, not a hole in the wall: its floor is laid OVER the lobby floor (a
lobby seat and a secret seat may share a tile; the zone keeps them apart on screen), so the
grid does not change and nothing about the pit does. `use_door` (tag 17) flips a lobby seat
standing on `door_tiles` to `entry_tile` in ZONE_SECRET, and a secret seat on `exit_tiles`
back to `return_tile` in ZONE_LOBBY. gen_map.py compiles these into map.rs / map.ts as
SECRET_ROOM, SECRET_DOOR, SECRET_EXIT, SECRET_ENTRY, SECRET_RETURN and refuses a room off
the lobby floor, a door without wall to its west, or an exit off the room's east column;
gen_secret.py paints the chamber onto exactly `room_tiles` and proves `door_tiles` is the
painted arch in lobby.png.
